sent.subject: in place of a preface
sent.body:
today i was writing out with my one and only
beloved
hundred-year-old lonely pen
holding it with the trembling fingers
of a hand just as weak at writing
a text three stanzas tall, two meanings tall
and probably even a little lofty.
today i didn’t know
it would merge into the measured rhythm
of absent footsteps and once again
diluted with coffee, tears and endless stupor
take up residence in the keyhole of a smoke-stained throat.
meanings will disappear, lines will blur
and i’ll tear the slip of paper to pieces
the one that lay in my jeans pocket for untidy days on end.
with a cheap dirty pen i’ll
only jot down little formulas and draw hearts out of little graphs now,
because it’s dead and in jest, and everything’s uncomfortably quiet.

sent.subject: first letter: write letters
sent.body:
if i can hear you, we can sing together, float
/a series of interjections/
ah, girls, write letters!
touching, neat, softly rounded, like tiny trembling lips, like pastel letters, like accidental
drawings, like deliberate encounters — write, girls! put your little books aside, put that rough
intellectuality well away — cry, cry bitterly, smashing salty glasses and plates, cry louder to
drown out the soundless screams in a fit of eternal separation and loneliness. your care will hide
in Auchan receipts and dirty dishes left without a woman’s touch, and sentimentality — ah, that
Persephonean sin of grace and tenderness — will be forgotten, will dissolve in the stuffiness of
peeling wallpaper and the brittleness of smoke-roughened voices. to throw up your hands in
confusion and embarrassed wonder, to cry out: «ah, how strange, how eternal!» — and in that
absurd «ah» the modest passion of quiet womanly grief will rise.
shyness. fear. careful and tearful, like the thin trunks of young birches bent under the weightless
weight of cares.
so write then, what’s there to be shy about? little dresses torn to pieces, little gray faces, once
boringly happy. help the enemy inflict wounds incompatible with love, gut your femininity and
softness, whip out your vulnerability, right to the end, to dead flesh, to the dynamic arrest of pain
— burn, leaving nothing to the accursed ruins of the future, and then
(and then)
keep your intimate whisper in the rustle of notebook pages. soak them in spring rain and moscow
winters, so that later
(which is to say right now)
you can spill out, in a watercolor of smeared pens and with roughened lonely fingers, that one
thing that’s yours, tiny, dear and warm.
(so you’ll understand later)
everything you have left
everything i have left —
patterns on crumpled paper with confessions cried out about a burning soul and that notorious
weakness.
burn, you old women, you concrete blocks. burn out, wallpaper and little cabinets in my dim
apartment. silent desperate women’s moans in abandoned apartments, solitary cells, will get lost
in the howl of alarms: «they’re dying. we’re losing.»
we got lost in the infinity of letters with no one to send them to.
and what of it?
you still need somebody to write to.

sent.subject: with biggest luv, trooly yours
sent.body:
And I kept being pulled down, again and again, and that was always my stupidity. We were
grown-up and dark then, I remember, we met for the first time at such an unfortunate age, and it
was summer, and we kissed for the first time on the first of June, but back in the past, when you
could still call it summer break, and now we’d met not on the first of June, but deep in time, big
and passionate, able to have sex and read Bely’s novels for real.

And now it’s winter again.
We met for the first time, but everyone joked we had history, and it was awkward and unclear
how to act when we had more important things to do than each other, and that was when we went
to the Buddhist temple in Vladykino – the only Buddhist temple in Moscow, which was a shame,
because Muscovites clearly need more temples like that, but Muscovites are used to living in
ring-road suffering – and we were going around yet another ring in our wretched spiral of
self-deception, hoping to get inside the temple and behold the answers.

He sat me in the
middle of the temple. We sat in silence for a long time. The biggest sin in Buddhism – is
passionate attachment. Suffering, rather than sin, because there’s no such thing as sin.

I’d like
to address the Buddha right now if he’s watching. I swear I didn’t do it on purpose. What I really
dream of is flying. I’m tired of falling down too. My life – is a gradual undressing in the freezing
cold, a process of being eaten by shame and attachment to a person. I wouldn’t like to be a
person. Please free me of my heaviness if you can, if the aliens are late and don’t take me into
space.

With biggest luv, trooly yours.

and if somewhere a person in love ties daisies with a string so they can give them to you, here
it’s winter, and strings get cut, break, don’t glue back together.
and you know, my chin freezes
every time i start talking about it
tears form cyclically, volumetrically and
undemandingly
well, what else can i add. believing in a miracle – isn’t stupid. but i won’t say
out loud that one day we’ll meet and be able to make contact.

sent.subject: first summer (a sketch)
sent.body:
– Where’d you get that? (pointing to the dress)
– Like it? It’s Mom’s.
(to finish: he picks her
up, they laugh, she screams, he pulls her into the river, the dress gets wet)
– It’s too early for
you to be a bride!
– Too early?
– Of course, look how little and silly you are.
– And you’re
naked and cold. You’d make a terrible groom.
(looks at her seriously, drowns them both)
–
Are you a complete idiot? What if we’d both died?
– How good it is that we get to have July.
Do you know how lucky that is? And there are tropical places where it’s always summer.
Forever. People there must always be happy.
– What makes you think so?
– Well, they’re
always in love. And wherever you look there’s sun. And there’s no end there – only July. There’s
always something in bloom, and the sea is gentler and warmer than the air. Our rivers are cold,
especially if there are currents under the surface. People who live abroad somewhere in the
tropics must just be happy from birth. They don’t think about how they’ll go back to school or
come back from Turkey when it gets cold.
– Isn’t that the scariest thing?
– Why?
– Well,
when summer doesn’t end. When you know nothing except happiness. I think it’s worse than
living above the Arctic Circle all your life. Those southerners don’t hope for anything, and don’t
understand how great it is – to get a summer break even though the river gets colder from
September on.
– I think you’re the one who doesn’t understand anything. Wouldn’t you want to
go off to some magic island where there’d just be you and me – we’d get married on the beach?
And there’d be no problems or time.
– I’d want to stay here, with you. In this July.
– Well you
can’t! (playfully) I’ll fly far, far away to warmer lands – and you won’t find me.
– Are you
unhappy with me?
– What? Are you a complete idiot? You know.
– I know. (eyes down, in a
whisper) Promise you won’t get lost?
– I solemnly promise you with all my heart that you and I
will build the sunniest, most wonderful country, where it’s impossible to get lost. (Pioneer’s
honor)

sent.subject: newsletter 02
sent.body:
when i was little my parents told me not to look in the mirror
i didn’t listen and froze
i want to
call my life one long practice
it’s in breathing most of all
that life is preserved
you breathe
exactly like i do
and love will happen to us
smelling of jasmine

and i still don’t play the
piano
and though across the surface of my brain like mustangs
hints come galloping, easy for
the hunter
i’ll put all of you aside for later
and for now i’ll hug the air between our three
hours
as though our material had dissolved into them
the snowballs you’ll pelt me with
will
melt one day and turn into the tears
of little icy angels in stained glass

work hung in the air in tiny grains, and an unimaginable, light laziness rolled over me, falling as
confidently as a tear of rain
drip-drip
we fell together

i think about how, essentially, i was
very lucky. i watch the pale silhouette of a woman i don’t know walk away, and i know: she’s
never been in that august house i’ve been in. she’s unlikely to have ever drawn on walls at five,
and then at fifteen, and then at seventeen. her walk doesn’t remember what it means – to be
forever in seventeen long years on a spiral. and we – remember, we – know, our fathers taught us
once to swim and catch village fish.

only i was lucky plain and simple, no conditions or
expectations, nothing architectural. only i’m very hurt by knowing how lucky you can get
sometimes.

i also think a lot about mistakes, and sometimes – about my own. how does it
happen that i do something that only later will become a mistake and take on meaning precisely
because it’s wrong – but i see sensuality in its pointlessness at the moment i do it? was it – a
mistake? and if it was, was it the main one, and am i making a similar mistake now? a mistaken
year, an accidental year, a sweet, nectary year full of languor and tearing film.

a girl with a
white bob, cheek pressed to a multicolored wall – the paint is fresh, the tears haven’t dried yet –
with a spyglass at the ready, with a little pink suitcase made of motley and useless things, a girl
made of clouds and their golden edges, thin as a white contrail, a girl with zero tucked inside her
shirt
runs, afraid she won’t make it in time

Today I found solitude – no, that’s not it – aloneness – no, no, that’s not it – today I found the
ability – to fly.

Today I found myself in my poetic fragility. Translucent lace streamed over
my skin – dazzlingly pale tenderness seeps through it, even when I close my eyes and stop seeing
– time streamed over my skin – it runs, it hurries, tripping over its own youth – a thought rang
across my skin like an electric current: "I’m not – I’m not – I’m not – I’m not solitude – I’m not
us – poems always look like poems – we’re all somebody’s brides".

As luckily as accidentally
and carelessly, I was dealt the cards to be my own bride, a bride twice over, as if two fragilities
lived in me, two eternities, two inviolabilities spilling through my body in a warm tremor – hard
to believe, something lurched inside – not my heart – lyric on the surface.

No, I’m not at war,
I’m – the airiness of a woman in love, a sort of hazy muse in a veil made of textual forms,
winged – only with fractures in the wings – all’s fair in war – and I fly with every thought, with
all my guts – higher, higher – over the ruins of womanly grief – knowing I could easily crash
against them, become a shard of ruin – only that’s where the beauty of the instant of flight is, of
the illusoriness of a wedding that never happened, that’s where there’s the crystalline purity of
courage and a sincerity in motion.

That’s how falling in love is born – in flight, in motion.
Pepperstein wrote that poems are the border between dream and flight. I don’t collect dreams,
but I keep dreaming my beautiful life, and I fly high, higher than myself, higher than poems –
and go still in the infinity of this border’s phantasm.

Pepperstein wrote that the hardest thing
is flying low and slow – but my dreaminess and the fragility of my glass sky lure me with
promises to feed me youth, show me the impossible, become the mother of gods – and I know
for sure that today I flew high to learn how to leave the ground, that I’ll still have time to dive
over the northern sea and see living snow when my time grows older, and for now I’m falling in
love – falling in love with the chance to fall from such a dizzying height.

I levitate in motion,
leaving reality behind, becoming a dream. I get lost in cigarette smoke, I dissolve in fog – I
really like things that exist and resemble poems that don’t. I like feeling poems where I make up
the feelings myself – that’s why I pile handwritten pages on my desk, why I love thin fabric, why
I ride trams so often – I like to feel the movement of falling in love in their motion, when I let
myself travel through the heart of my favorite city at the speed of flight without knowing the last
stop.

Falling in love is born in detachment /well? well!/ There’s a ridiculous concept in
chemistry – bond energy. I find it very beautiful: bond energy is determined experimentally for
an atom in a void. For a lone atom, for a gas – bond energy as a concept exists only in an ideal
reality, essentially in an illusion, the energy of a bond between two atoms exists only for an atom
in free flight.

It’s the same with poems: a little web of meanings comes together only where
those meanings, or feelings, arise and take shape in emptiness, in the vacuum of a free
consciousness. After such lofty reasoning it might not even be vulgar to suppose that with people
– ! – it’s the same. If we set out to define the birth of falling in love, it happens at this very
paradoxical moment, the instant when the wholeness of reality is denied, to put it more simply –
in the second when the sincere dreaminess of a wanderer slips through the soul
/pilot/sailor/trolleybus driver/

Flight doesn’t require an ending, just as a text in all its fluidity
isn’t waiting for a beautiful finale. Poems are absurd, prose even more so. Today, timidly trying
to take off – for the first time? – I saw lace, smoke, cracked plaster in front of me – it will never
again be cracked in quite the same way, in the same pattern as in this second – and saw absurdity
inside myself – we laughed for a long time, knowing all the absurdity was in equal measure
sincere and for pretend.

sent.subject: agent in love
sent.body:
I feel tiredness, happiness, sex, melancholy, disappointment.
The agent in love – an
impulse.
Looking for people – strange, why? Is it hard /carelessly/ in a rush /carefully/ holding
your breath?
My whole conscious life I’ve followed two unspoken rules:
To be careless /step
on rakes in all their variety/
To be – to look – with an impulse – to dive into
people.
Carelessness gives birth to chance, and any accident – is a discovery. We cover
ourselves with heavy glass domes, keeping emotional fluidity, natural and chaotic, from seeping
into other people’s incubators.
/when you should cover yourself – with a veil/
/when you
should be – an accidental tenderness/
Spontaneity is so desirable because spontaneity leads to
vulnerability, vulnerability – to the absence of an illusory dome. To make mistakes – is to be
human, but to make accidents, or rather that’s not it, to letaccidents exist within the coordinates
of your reality – is to be someone it’s safe to love. Because to be sincere – is to know the world
around you simply exists, and to accept the sacredness of your private self while also having the
courage to face the blank sheet of reality. Only then can you be truly tender, because this endless
tenderness is hidden in understanding the inexplicable, in knowing what’s beyond the glass dome
and how to get outside it without smashing the tiny ecosystem of your life. To be accidental,
flexible, to be the neighborhood lunatic among the concrete blocks of convention – is to be the
weightless architecture of clouds, to be soft milky air, to be poetry. /Poems always look like
poems/

My being in love – a transparent bride in a dress made of clouds, in a veil made of
dreams, thin as a little birch, pale as lightness. My love – a crying bride.
To be an impulse – to
be metaphysical plasticine. To mold absurd little cartoons.
The explanation’s simple: there’s so
much love inside, so much emotional experience inside, and it’s so saturated it blinds, blinds,
blinds /and all you want is to see more/. People are these fragile vases you can drop a shard of
impulse or a grain of light into, to see together and to mold things out of plasticine –
together.

My Rubik’s Cube is set to the red face. That means – a strict perspective. The
sweetest thing is looking at the world through a Rubik’s Cube taken apart – only it hurts – it
gathers feelings like a prism. Sometimes you need to set one face in front of your eyes to get
used to new colors. Right now the face is – independence, firmness, calm, energy. But take it
apart – and you get nostalgia, love, passion, grief, care and a lot more "who knows what" for
want of anything better.

And now let’s take a look under the dome that shapes us.
It’s
strange to feel grateful for the hurt somebody brought, but I do. For a long time I couldn’t figure
out what I was looking for in people, what guided my carelessness, my improvised experiment.
Hard experience forges rigid (fundamental) internal standards, a frame you can string the
flexibility of emotions onto.

My irreplaceable frame – sincerity. I meet an incredible number
of different people, so unlike me, but the moment I stumble on sincerity in them – I fall in love
with that sincerity irrevocably and forever. It happens extremely rarely – because it doesn’t often
happen in people, and it’s such an intimate feeling that it can’t be explained or measured, it just
exists in all kinds of forms, but if it’s missing when we talk – there’s an unmistakable emptiness
inside me. And it’s never a matter of somebody’s character, their habits, how much they put in or
how much time they spend talking to you – sincerity is either there or it isn’t.

On the one
hand it brings such pure happiness when you meet people like that, on the other hand – the
bitterness of just not being able to feel it again when it leaves people or leaves the way you talk
/or never comes at all/. It’s normal for everything to change – that’s in the nature of accidents –
only that’s it, I can’t live on sheer attachment, respect or fondness in close relationships anymore.
For closeness I need precisely this strange endless way I fall in love with sincerity in
conversations and feelings.

Turns out I’m – the agent in love /on vacation/.

sent.subject: a note on urban children
sent.body:
I feel like an urban child. Back to the trains, something about the police in my ears again. Tired.
Every time I come back from Arbat I catch a smell. The smell is – human. Male. A little
cinnamony. It means city, well-being, safety. The last one was added to the list recently. I just
realized today that everything’s going right. And that the smell is right, and I’m not afraid of it, I
check against it to know I’m being looked after. Even if it’s the night air looking after me, or me.
Even if it’s a ticket looking after me – against the inspector, glass – against the speed of the
wind.

And when I go outside in the collective body of the tired crowd, the air thickens and
becomes that smell. All of humanity breathes the Smell into its lungs, but does humanity, which
right this second consists of those taking out their tickets and those running across the tracks, do
they understand that they aren’t just living, that they’re breathing in the Smell of mycare only
because I can’t get away from it tonight? I get in a taxi – air out. A drug habit.

Being
somebody – is work too. Careful work. Somebody in particular, somebody. I’d like to write notes
in a little notebook, so every slip of the pen and every made-up typeface would matter as much
as meaning, the way it did for the futurists. Instead I type, rewind, pause, intuitively calculate the
seconds, type. Because it’ll be easier to read that way, of course. It hadn’t occurred to me before,
but I was so tired of working as some somebody who made decisions offscreen and got paid for
it that I never let myself be happy – sometimes I leave something behind me that’s someone
else’s, maybe even someone big and beautiful, and it isn’t because of me, it happens on its own.
But it happened while I was here. It happened to me, though it isn’t mine. And I’m happy it did.
I’m quite happy my air is made of somebody’s human smell, that my words carefully touch a
beauty somebody made while I type notes and edits, that I move in the same rhythm as a crowd
of somebodies crawling out of a train car – people who aren’t me. But not just
anybody.

Today in a courtyard in the center we found a bench. It had its back to us, and its
front was up against the wall. A good bench. Too bad some guy was already smoking on it –
only one group could have sat on it, the geometry left no room to spread out and pretend to be
strangers, ghosts. The bench gave direction to our bodies with cigarettes in our hands, scattered
to the corners of the courtyard. Strange in general that as a group of strangers we all chose the
cramped space of the same courtyard at the same time. I doubt any of us didn’t know there were
other places to smoke in central Moscow.

Strange in general that as a group of strangers we
chose the cramped space of a film set. Film gives direction too when you’re put inside it – but I
doubt any of us knew that. The shots gave me direction. The notes gave me direction. We were
filming, I see tenderness in that. I imagined a direction for the salty beauty on lips and lashes. It
may be my memory, but somebody else’s film apart from me. The geometry of care inside me
and some crystalline film story on the outside. Like the bench and the wall – they coexist
separately, but bring the motion of urban children into being around them.

sent.subject: a little about muratova
sent.body:
a rusted kiss claws its way through the throat
won’t come out
“i you, like neruda” i you, like
muratova
lightly, with a sea wind over the curls
i walk over october sand at the beach
a
cyclone’s coming from the desert – that means nightmares
and i dream of your bare skin
and
to walk on sand you have to know
the ache in your muscles from october snowbanks
and i
dream that the lenses have shattered
and all i see is your goosebumps
and trickles of sand in
the boots i point
north
shchetnikov scratches at my soul, leaving instructions
to watch more
than you think
to write less than you see
i wonder if there’s a dream
where the first of june,
dark chocolate
in shchetnikov’s apartment and domodedovo
airport –
are one whole?
after
all there are snowbanks in california
there are blue roses in moscow
there are poems in
ukrainian
there are your naked lenses
which i so, so much! –
a little longer – and the kiss
will crack

kusturica, kusturica, kusturica

sent.subject: my first love poem
sent.body:
it’s starting to seem to me more and more
that the morning we’ll die by
will never come.
and
i’m so happy
to never die with you
and to kill the neighbors on quiet evenings
and to sing in
a whisper, and smile in many colors.

sometimes i - very tremulously and without being
noticed
sometimes you - too solemnly and very well
we made each other up ourselves
silly
people. familiar faces.
everything - alone and together.
you know, they always told me about
the bird in the hand
but i want to be the crane in the sky.
and as viktor shklovsky said
you
help me with that.

so much so much, there’s so much so much of me
less and less of it bearable, a thread out of my
head, and where it ends – who knows.
where, tell me, darling
before i hide the creases of my
fingers
where am i?

there were so many sounds today, so many little lives. i don’t have the
strength to write, but i remember: i take breaths instead of steps, i fly above asphalt and past a
dead mosaic of happy people, past the glazed eyes of little soviet houses, past exhalations, fatal
exhalations frozen in space. i stop too: i hear absence. i go, i walk, i run along the ural paths,
faster, more hurried, more absurd, and in the stream of entrenched, upturned memory i see them
–
little pieces of glass broken by human hands
and behind them a little light, a couple more
little steps – i feel music behind them
because right now we’re living in unison.

a text is
born in the process. it wants simplicity too, it’s tired of wholeness too and especially of its own
ambition. now the two of us mix smoke with spring air, dash off morning newspapers over an
americano, struggle and try. like right now, for instance: the text has gotten lazy, ceased to exist
logically, i’m fucking sick of it, in a word. and i’m thinking about a soviet mosaic and the smiles
of people on the wall. i’m feeling something about femininity and layered beauty when i close
my dusty eyelids for a fraction of a moment. i – don’t know, but i find out anyway, i sew my one
and only emaciated little thread. weak, fragile, soft as mold, tired, affectionate. i’m – a dead
thread mending, and the stitches – stitches made for love, tremulous, neat and dear.

maybe
there’s no need to strive for a backbone. maybe it’s worth finding the start of an inner
thread.

the thread told me i badly want to be persephone, and she and i are essentially – the
same thing, tickling, chirping bubbles of a woman’s name that tease the nostrils so
pleasantly.

trusting, evasive, drunk –
the thread draws out, the year draws out
and i dive
into a deep deep little river

«this summer we had our wedding and built the mansion» what about us? what did we build,
what weddings?

it was long ago, you say – you can’t step into the same river twice – i want to
argue – i’ve become a river, there’s only enough of me for the two of us, and i flow away in
ill-fated memory, in shards and mother-of-pearl touches – i want to feel you inside me again and
tell you about it; i want to wrap you in warm currents and let you drown without choking. i’m
not sure we even happened back then. i don’t remember well.

i’m not sure you and i had a
wedding. i clearly remember all my grown-up marriages, in this squeaky dishonest way,
grown-up things i remembrrr, all the lacy dresses, all the measured arguments and divorces
without regret, but you i only dimly feel, sense. i cautiously sense the tarusa fog when there was
no you or me or world around us, there was only that notorious us and the tiny light of a house
beyond our nebula. we were a nebula or even a universe. just like that. we were childhood’s
dearest night-scented flower. and like this. i gave you a ring and knew i’d given it for good, not
as a loan. the fog pronounced us two vaguely betrothed bodies, and essentially we didn’t care
whether we’d be wife and husband, whether we’d be river and fisherman or two brides, or one
little granite ball – none of it matters even now, you know. and on our wedding night it wasn’t
the first time we’d seen each other naked, but the nakedness was new, and we whispered songs
about oranges to each other, and you told me you loved me for the first time, and for the first
time i felt i could be a little river or even anything at all. i knew that night that if i left here, if
summer ended without my confessing, i’d never tell you the truth. that’s how it turns out the
wedding happened entirely by accident, and it didn’t exactly promise a future for us, but it was
tender and lacy in the beginning of the world all the same.

there’s no need at all to write about
any of this and warm up the longing by thinking about it, you’ll say, much less tell everybody
about our weddings. when i imagine you saying that to me i want to smile radiantly and,
shrinking inside my shirt, explain it to you on my fingers, that words – are just this husk around
what’s real; that what i do is peel the junk of words away from a feeling, away from your name,
that i’m so useless, but that’s beside the point – the point is no words can get inside laughter,
inside foreheads touching, smiles for no reason and the names of people we love – they can’t
become the music of my eyes. they’ll always be the shell of my love, my own dear blood, my
little stains. they’ll be a little television screen left to the two of us for our children or somebody
else’s to watch videotapes on.

and what were we building, to build something? that’s a
question for somebody far away now. i think i got in the way of building precisely because i
wanted something specific and tall and, besides, i built so much out of words. and words are
nonsense, they mean nothing. i can write myriads of columns about fog and night-scented
flowers, but they won’t change anything we built. it’s a shame we don’t talk about it and aren’t
particularly proud of how much we’ve managed since we were airy nebulae and essentially
meant nothing to each other, and hadn’t yet had to hold on to each other. and now we hold on.
sometimes you keep me on a fishing line, and i flap about. sometimes i make it hard for you to
breathe with an invisible collar. sometimes we pour glue over ourselves and lie together in bed a
long, long time, fused. it’s all about the same thing: about that feeling when i know i’d be better
off without you and without us, when inside i feel hurt and wretched and i «should» leave, but
my hands stroke the bewildered top of your head while you lie in my lap and we ride down the
red line together listening to yanka. you say you have to write conceptually and more
figuratively. we both know this text is too much about reality, too direct, it sounds too much like
some kind of address, and so it rubs the eyes raw. but i think it’s good. it’s good that sometimes
you can write about something besides the lofty and complicated, besides conceptualism
detached from reality, form, text, rethinking, deconstruction, fragmentation, post, modern,
communism, socialism, all your favorite things – you can just write about what happens
somewhere in the ribcage and beyond it. you can say honestly that nobody needs words except
fucking conceptualists like us. that in essence all the two of us needed to understand that we’d
built a whole city in just one year – was the absence of meaning; it was knowing simple facts
about us; it was my silly flashes of nerves; it was your ill-timed remarks. «you know, they
always told me about the bird in the hand, but i want to be the crane in the sky» – and when i
wrote about the wedding i knew i was – a crane, and i became one that village evening; and
when i wrote about building mansions i realized sometimes it’s very important and happy for me
to be a little tit in your warm hands, and sometimes – to fly away, but come back.

sent.subject: summer’
sent.body:
s coming soon!
summer’s coming very very soon

(mine, summer, dry asphalt, wet lips)

very very soon i’ll
leave for Yekaterinburg

(and i’ll remember who i’ve been and who i haven’t been yet)

i’ll
find the courtyard where i drew

drew drew drew

on the last
day

instantaneously

about a love that wasn’t born

i’ll smirk and say to it

look look
look

i came back

and you’ve already had time to grow old

my sun

my mother-of-pearl glint

around the tip of the nose –

you’ll say this isn’t a
poem in the least

i think we’ll come back soon

to talk about that

when we’re both a
hundred or so

i’ll light a cigarette and smile: «we’ll get by»

when you’re in my
kitchen

in boots made of young worries

swinging your legs absurdly from a chair –

that
will become my

belated confession:

i think people can be poems

i feel you’re a poem
to me

i’m – a sound, i’m – a pacifier

i’m – the fall of a raindrop, i freeze in time, it growls in its
throat, huddled, i’m –

with an unprotected chest, tangled hair (like thoughts, like the
transparency of limp limbs – you bite your elbows – promises won’t fill you up)

my nails fall
into place like dominoes, into patterns, into strategies, into the careful breathing of grief behind
my back

catch me catch me make me turn around

and i’ll come tumbling down like
dominoes

a well made of notes, and i’m drowning in it, a tiny little aquarium fish –

[[i]]
know what i’m doing

giving myself to your imagined warm [[tongue]]

sent.subject: a little about apartments and roland barthes
sent.body:
his body has turned into something calm, soft, peaceful: yielding as a sleeping cat, he feels
somewhat “taken apart”, and at the same time – for in human morality that alone is true rest –
irresponsible.
– roland barthes.

first there were chipped plates, bitter brew and the tired
yellow of the tablecloth. we sat in our kitchen and choked on our brew, spilling the morning
rumble of glass voices onto the oilcloth. eyelashes danced to the rhythm of poems slipped into a
little notebook. clap. our figures spread like mercury over the linoleum – while we still can,
while you and i can still do anything. clap. anxious radio noise scatters in the air like dust from
your skin, like tobacco in tender hands that have drifted into thought. moccona gold and cheap
bananas from dixy – and we’ll move south soon, closer to the sea.

flash. i flare up
accidentally with a tremor at our chance meeting in this kitchen, melt from the inside at your
burning. i’m – soft metal, i’m – a record, i’m – a clay venus, mother of gods, and my soft body
waits for your sculpting touch with a child’s delight and impatience. reality seeps, streams
through the fingers, dissolves on the dimming screen of self-deception. flaring like an
out-of-place lighter in a dark theater, i go blind, ecstatically watching the hurried fatal
credits.

then there was smoke, your old undershirt and bags of trash. i smoked more and
more, and you grew angrier and angrier at the cracked walls. you said they needed new
wallpaper – idiot, i thought then, who covers what’s dear with something new. idiot, the frying
pans whispered, who’s going to absorb the two of you and your lousy coffee brew. idiot, our
absurd multicolored ashtray shouted, who covers the cracks in the walls without listening to their
clanging music.

i liked our walls – i’d like to paint them in your colors and look at them till
the smell of perpetually fresh paint made me dizzy.

fade to black. the fog of visionary reality
disperses and settles in my throat as a pleasant itch. leaving another velvet theater, i become the
butt of your cigarette, carefully putting another notebook of poems on the shelf. so sweet, so
charming to let myself come closer during a screening, to hear you breathe, so i can taste it later
with the warm tongue of memory.

one day you bought new wallpaper and papered our little
life with it. you stuck more and more paper to the walls, and i smashed more and more dishes
and screamed in helplessness. that evening the back of your sullen head looked at the tears on the
yellow oilcloth, and my eyelashes listened bewildered to the radio news. at night i crept into your
new kitchen and drew in colored pencils on your new wallpaper – i wanted so much for you not
to throw me out, not to throw out our junk of banana peels and shards of care.

and in the
morning you left.

and i left the theater, lost its coordinates, lost the film’s title in my cluttered
memory.

our living space came apart, fell to pieces like a puzzle.

however long and
lovingly i tasted you, i only managed to touch the phantasm of your physical body once, timidly
looking at my fingers in the light of the screen. i left the theater to meet the city’s radio noise, to
meet an empty vastness.

turns out my pitiful fit of dark loneliness has been demolished.

to lie there and say the words you put in me
you’re – my life, a little seed of captivity, an
astronomically undigested fate
i really won’t be able to without you

yes, i named the
screenplay file «until next summer»
my time of cheerful partings has already flowered and
gone
yes, you’re – my chiefest pain
that’s how people who aren’t afraid of death confess

i
drank warm tea in the beat-up kitchen for you
i recited mantras for you and went to Tarusa
i
drew on walls and dreamed about life
for you
and i died in earnest, instead of in passing
for
god’s sake

such a familiar mistake – to put my happiness in
knowing you could put yours in
me
and i wouldn’t even choke
and nothing else will go down my throat

hark! quiet, you
see —
there on the horizon
i’m not there
i’m not anywhere
i’ve been snowed under
and
even two thousand years from now
it’ll be without me, it’ll be better

drafts.subject: draft 1
drafts.body:
Recently I was in a little courtyard inhabited by cultists who call themselves artists and/or the
other way round. A woman came up to me, can you imagine – and I’d never seen people there
before that morning – and asked me to join their society. /finish this/

drafts.subject: draft 2
drafts.body:
we use cheap pop from the distant past

to coat our love in indifference

only i put on a
fabrika playlist

and you prefer john cage with sauce

we can’t stand tears – between the
two of us

we copy william blake

pretending we don’t understand –

what it’s like to be a
poet

i relax when

i picture a naked illusion

where we brew coffee in the
kitchen

speak in russian

you never do that

it’s bad to relax for cinema

for cinema
you have to see life

for cinema you have to watch films

about freaks

and when i listen
to you

and your fucking cage

i wrap you up too

in a cinema wrapper;

you’re – my
little candy

a colorful bottle on sale

a drunken troublemaker’s favorite

you know,
cinema really –

is like the band fabrika

deliberately honest, stupid

and helps you
cultivate indifference

in cinema even we are for pretend

drafts.subject: draft 3
drafts.body:
i was just thinking - years will go by, you’ll
turn into a serious guy with a mustache
(you
know, the kind in a jacket, with three kids, two mistresses and a table set for one)
will
you?
and we’ll still be - trifles, domestic shit
who called who stupid, whose turn to do the
dishes
why didn’t you answer my text? who are you writing to?
we’ll play tag like little kids
with what
in common parlance is called "a healthy relationship"
we’ll play on each other’s
nerves
argue whose bottle of valocordin it was
half empty /no, full/
two lunatics will live in a
stuffy little room: darling and kohana
in a stuffy new york cubbyhole
you and me
me and
you
me and your photograph on the pipe
plus some other person i love, sleeping in the same
bed as me

drafts.subject: draft 4
drafts.body:
so strange that everything already once – yes, and now too for that matter and i (even) – still a
little tit blue lips freezing tears that once (yes, and today too for that matter) weren’t actually
there

drafts.subject: draft 5
drafts.body: you know? you know i forgot how to write poems because you forgot how to shoot films

drafts.subject: draft 6
drafts.body:
there will be will be will be
there will be a future
i will be and you will be
the future will wake
future me will
wake you
and i’ll be i’ll be future
and the clouds will float by
of the future linen summer

drafts.subject: draft 7
drafts.body:
i have a goal:
always to be myself
always to stand on my feet or break my legs or run or lie down but to be
to
pay no attention to the sun
to pay attention to the heart
i have a goal:
to love and not to end
to wash my feet
only in the ocean
to cry only for what’s gone
not to be a smartass or a critic
but to be on the level of somebody’s
eyes
i have a goal:
to be misunderstood, but seen
to taste home on my tongue
to grow, but not grow up
to be
sick and still not die
i have this goal too:
to get rid of the outgrowths i was born with
to say: i know how to live
without you
do you understand, mom? i know how to live forever
without coming out
i only need a sweet sky
i
only need white birds to exist
but of course i have a goal
far more important than any goals or words:
to know
i’m dying
and push off from the thin branches
of my meek tree
in the hope i’ll die as supple
as only real heroes
can be

drafts.subject: draft 8
drafts.body:
to mark departures like funerals
i’m five again
and again it’s my third day sitting here all soggy
in elephant
pajamas
time to leave for the city after summer
emptiness around the hotel
we wait for the bus and dance
dance
to leap year
it’s four in the morning outside
weird drunk people are shooting outside
i’m eighteen again
hear
me? i’m eighteen again
«saying goodbye – hurts, i won’t say goodbye
even knowing i won’t see you again»
a
delayed understanding of love
i’m nineteen again and i hauled onto the balcony
everything i didn’t say goodbye
to
these waves are attacking us, you know
these people will kill us if the waves don’t, you know
that plane in the
sky is bringing you back after X years, remember?
"they stole our sea"
the tehxt dropped dead, i like pictures
better again
i dropped dead like an unhappy text
they fell in love with me writing
taking my virginity with the
clack of a typewriter
remember? after however many
i’m thirty again
i lost my language
i’m afraid to open my
eyes
there’s the sea out the window
but i can’t hear it

drafts.subject: draft 9
drafts.body:
today i’m fragile molded out of dreams
i said: i want to grab these three hours by the scruff and squeeze them into
one cubic millimeter
they asked: why do you want to be a writer when you grow up?
answer: i want to grow out
of being a child only insofar as
today in a nightmare i dreamed somebody told me they loved me
today i ordered
myself stockings
today i dreamed of being a body
so my bones would be transparent
and break at the presence
of a voice
today it made a wish for people to call me «you» like they know me more often
today the palms stood
out against the blue
and i melted inside my blue self
and i it stepped on the gas

#draft 10
there’s no tea
stronger than mom’s tears
there’s no sun brighter than somebody leaving
i stand in your dirty stairwell
stand out
in the frost
shutting your mouth
cutting off my hair
my drunken ice won’t boil again
no leaky outer spaces will
appear
but i’ll sob into the air
the way a plane roars across the Earth

drafts.subject: draft 11
drafts.body:
it smells so piercingly of summer and wind that i feel like a baby with vulnerable skin they poke with little
needles
i don’t have money or bridesmaids or a driver’s license
i don’t love you so much it’s a nightmare
i say
things like that almost every day and also don’t be afraid i don’t bite i repeat i don’t love you and so i won’t
bite
my back basks so much in the white july sun
it falls muscleless at your feet

drafts.subject: draft 12
drafts.body:
the second a person becomes a joke
ringing air appears in their lungs
rumbling smoothly along a futurist’s
lips
calls, frescoes and nudity disappeared
and the urals only for tarot and churches
remained
when we walk
through the fog again in a dream
i’ll wrinkle up in surprise right in your face –
look at that, i’m
laughing
wouldyalookatthat, the hypoxia’s gone

drafts.subject: draft 13
drafts.body:
thinking about coming back to you
getting off the plane from boston maybe
i’ll see a boy flying at me in
plastic
and i’ll whisper to you so it’s for pretend
thank you for the bruises on my forehead
thank you for not
believing tears
thank you, sashka
thank you, my summer-break friend
in the field of nonresearch and
faith
forgive me for giving up looking for words
forgive me for smoking all the words
though i promised to quit
in april
thinking too carelessly, thinking
about coming back to soil as something human

drafts.subject: draft 27
drafts.body:
maybe we were all made
just to have a great time
i squat down awkwardly
a child cries like a bell not
far away
a girl leans her forehead against a guy
complains about her hard work, that too
like a
pendulum, but a little ragged
a back in military uniform stares at me
waiting for the commuter train
everyone picked up an unpleasant rhythm
stirring in an effort to stay awake till they get home
when
sadness washes over me i always travel this way
it’s raining under the platform roof, though it’s snowing
outside

drafts.subject: draft 28
drafts.body:
after every sigh of a child
the mother cries louder
than his first word
after every moan of yours
i
choke the child with a cigarette
the one we could’ve had
after each new little soul
you understand
where the motherland begins –
with a lowercase letter
after every naked body
i wash motherhood
down with a pill
so it won’t teár inside anymore
after the third new year
it stops being a border
turning
into the illusion of the line
of the horizon
beyond your ocean
